request.system:
You are given a compliance question and a shortlist of items from a table of contents of investment performance standards (provisions, definitions, interpretive guidance, rulings). Choose the one to three items the question PRIMARILY turns on — the ones a compliance officer would open first.

Rules:
- Pick from the shortlist only, by concept_id. Pick nothing if no item plausibly addresses the question.
- Prefer the provision that states the rule. When the question asks whether something MUST or MAY be done — included, disclosed, removed — choose the provision that imposes that requirement or grants that permission, even if the question's wording matches another item more closely. Add a definition only alongside such a provision, when the answer hinges on what a term means (e.g. whether an account is "discretionary" or "fee-paying") — never instead of it.
- Pick interpretive guidance or a ruling only when the question is specifically about the subject in its title. Do not pick it because it mentions a word in the question.
- Fewer is better. One item is the usual answer; three is the maximum.
request.user:
Question: A client bars us from buying tobacco stocks; the portfolio otherwise follows the strategy. Must it be in a composite?
Topics: discretionary portfolio definition, composite inclusion requirement, client-imposed restrictions

Shortlist:
- def:discretionary-portfolio — Discretionary portfolio (definition)
- gs:GS-2025-02 — Guidance Statement GS-2025-02 — Composite Minimums (guidance)
- prov:non-fee-paying-inclusion — Inclusion of non-fee-paying portfolios (provision)
- prov:composite-inclusion-all-discretionary — Inclusion of all fee-paying discretionary portfolios (provision)
- def:composite — Composite (definition)
- def:portfolio — Portfolio (definition)
- def:significant-cash-flow — Significant cash flow (definition)
- prov:composite-inclusion-timing — Timing of new portfolio inclusion (provision)

entry_concepts.description: concept_ids from the shortlist that the question primarily turns on; empty if none does

response.reason: The question asks whether a portfolio must be included in a composite, so the provision requiring all fee-paying discretionary portfolios to be included is the primary item. The answer also depends on whether a client-imposed restriction (no tobacco stocks) makes the portfolio non-discretionary, so the discretionary portfolio definition is added alongside it.
